title: Prove binary E8 factor-rank-sum barrier 21 at every term count
body:
## Summary

Scoped proof from cited geometric premises: for the fixed 120-line binary E8 matrix `K(q,r)=1+(q dot r)/2 mod 2`, every finite binary factorization whose actual factor-rank sum is at most 20 has rational pairing-rank cost at least 72. This extends Ali Romman's #4967 eleven-term obstruction to arbitrary term counts in the stated rank classes.

```text
K = A B^T over F2, rank(A)+rank(B) <= 20
  duplicate merging + cited coset/basis bounds + product rank
  => rational root-pairing cost >= 72 for any finite term count
```

For reduced rank-(10,10) factorizations, the stronger bound is `8m-16`, hence at least 80 at twelve terms. A twelve-term saving can therefore occur only at rank pairs (9,12), (10,11), (11,10), or (12,9). These four pairs remain open.

Only `research/e8-one-extra-direction/` is added. The binary factorization, rational pairing charge and full fixed root set are explicit in PROOF.md. The result was produced by Nick Petalas. Ali Romman's geometric premises, conorholds' #3755 method antecedent, Joel Pulikkan / GamingPuzzled #620, DreamingOfClouds #446 and the retained E8 lineage keep their credit.

## Evidence

Before: #4967 bounds every factorization with at most eleven terms and leaves twelve terms open. Its one-coset defect and dimension-eleven basis theorems are cited premises, not replay targets.

After: the written normalization argument removes the term-count restriction for factor-rank sum at most 20. The independent six-line algebra fixtures pass 262,144 merge inequalities, 4,096 pairing inequalities, 8,192 complete operator/cost/rank normalization checks, 92 two-sided arithmetic cases, 69 one-sided cases and eleven controls. These fixtures corroborate the new algebra, not the E8 geometric premises.

Local CPython 3.12.15 on macOS 27.0.1 arm64:

- Both registered warnings-as-errors checks pass, normal and optimized, in 0.169 and 0.199 seconds respectively, rounded upward to milliseconds.
- Package metadata/source pins and full registered replay pass.
- Exact committed-byte/source-history check passes at `1fa430647d32f71a7ad20e1b2c27c1c6190abd3c`, covering all six package files and the canonical source ancestor.
- Isolated optimized replay from a read-only six-file Git-free export passes and leaves every byte unchanged.
- The verifier emits a generated receipt bound to all six package source hashes. No receipt is handwritten.

Exact reproduction from the repository root:

```sh

/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -I -B research/e8-one-extra-direction/verify.py

```

Another CPython 3.12 executable may replace the displayed interpreter path. Standard library only.

## Limitations

This is an algebraic scoped proof, not a complete multiplication theorem or a new kappa. The cited geometric premises retain their original author-checked status and were not independently reverified here. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. Masked/punctured matrices, odd-characteristic scalar factors, shared physical delivery, native callers, restoration and complete recursive invoices remain outside scope. No Lean build or historical supplier cold replay was run. The selected frontier is unchanged.

## Open next questions

- Resolve the twelve-term rank-(10,11)/(11,10) cases by coupling the three quotient-coset deficits on the larger side to the opposite one-coset budget.
- Resolve rank-(9,12)/(12,9) by extending the minimum-basis support-rank theorem to a dimension-twelve binary code extension. Neither follow-up is reserved.

## Related open work

No open PR located in the refreshed metadata targets this fixed binary matrix and the same factor-rank restriction. Nearby work uses different matrices, scalar fields or charges:

- #5064 changes masked rational E8 completions and searches nine-factor bases; this proof fixes the binary matrix and does not evaluate that search.
- #3045 studies square root-code decoders with arbitrary fitting binary charge tables; this result allows extra factor-space directions but fixes a different binary scalar-factorization problem and rational pairing charge.
- #3040 classifies rank-eight E8 zero-pattern realizations after deletions; no pattern rigidity or deletion result is claimed here.
- #2832 reduces the characteristic-zero decoder problem to its canonical rational matrix; its scalar field and charge differ from this binary theorem.
- #3074 prices one-sided P112-to-P120 padding for the rational L120 programme; this theorem does not discharge L120.
- #2985 closes residue cells for one-sided rational E8 lifts; this result does not replay or close any of those cells.
- #3029 studies a conditional P112 two-sided deficiency budget; no implication to that different model is asserted.
- #3154 collects conjectural dependencies for the P112 COPY floor; the binary rank-sum result does not close those conjectures.
- #3895 screens a complex rank-sixteen block decoder; its complete recursive bill is outside this scalar binary obstruction.

- #5154 proves a sharp 128 COPY floor for a specified two-call P112 exceptional-hull cross-form family. This result fixes a single 120-line binary E8 matrix and rational pairing charge; the numbers concern different contracts and are not compared.
